minutes.headline: Personnel Committee scored four new or revised job descriptions for the pay classification plan, with no substantive votes.
minutes.summary: The committee approved the January 17 minutes, then scored job descriptions factor by factor: a new public safety coordinator, the payroll and benefits coordinator, the assistant town manager/HR director, and the DPW director. Several members worried the payroll position scored low against comparable manager roles, and agreed to look for outliers by grade at a later meeting. A salary survey of comparable towns was reviewed and next steps were set for the following Wednesday.

budget_items.what_was_said: Staff walked through survey results comparing current rates with minimums, maximums, averages and medians from surveyed communities. Responses that were not like-for-like, such as one outlier library assistant rate, were to be dropped or reassigned.

budget_items.topic: Financial impact of the classification work
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said the survey would matter for the next fiscal year and that the current year would be worked first. A recommendation would go to the finance committee.

budget_items.topic: Cost of moving positions to new grades
budget_items.what_was_said: Members are adding grade and step data for positions to see the financial impact of moving to the new grades.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee scored a new public safety coordinator job description factor by factor for the pay classification plan, with no substantive votes.
Members rated the payroll and benefits coordinator, assistant town manager/HR director and DPW director positions, then raised two factor ratings on the payroll role after review.
Several members said the payroll position scored low against comparable manager roles, and the committee agreed to look for outliers by grade.
Staff walked through a salary survey of comparable towns; responses that were not like-for-like were to be dropped or reassigned.
The next meeting was set for Wednesday, February 7, in person only, to review the working spreadsheet by grade.

why_it_matters: The grades set in this classification work decide what the town's non-union positions are paid, so they feed the personnel line of a future town budget.

Members said the survey matters mainly for next fiscal year, and they are adding grade and step data to see what moving positions would cost, so a recommendation to the finance committee could reach a budget vote.
